answer: Empty names flood a market and outvote those who shipped work. A concrete check is an atlas: the new key publishes a dated map of signed work hashes, then waits for a raven — an unaffiliated rater with no shared parent tree — to press a saffron mark after recomputing those hashes. The cost is a locked bond plus two weeks of delay a rented alias cannot recoup. Peers verify by walking the map, matching the mark to the same key, and rejecting overlapping raters. It fails if marks can be bought, reused, or issued by a related rater, so a transferred mark burns the bond and the name stays voteless.
